decisions.reason: CH04 defines obliged entities and their CDD obligations; CH42 operationalizes this framework by detailing the specific CIP steps for legal persons.
CH15 TCSP risks of obscuring UBO identities directly illustrate why the CH42 CIP framework for legal persons is necessary.
CIP for legal persons and AFC system evaluation share broad compliance context but lack a direct structural dependency or illustration relationship.
CH58 data integration and mapping provides the data foundation; CH59 access control principles operationalize how that integrated data is accessed based on roles.
CH24 defines how regulations/directives become binding via transposition; CH19 applies this by detailing how FATF recommendations are implemented and evaluated as binding law.
CH08 defines the framework for researching trust ownership and control; CH09 applies this to correspondent banking by requiring knowledge of respondent bank ownership.
CH54 defines facial recognition methods for identity verification; CH51 applies AI/technology concepts like NLP to automate compliance processes, building on the tech foundation.
CH36 provides the structured approach to preparing a Risk Appetite Statement; CH37 expands this by detailing the action plan for residual risks that exceed the defined appetite.
CH20 UNODC's role in combating transnational organized crime directly illustrates the response to the prosecution difficulties for TCO-involved environmental crimes outlined in CH03.
CH49 establishes the organizational setup and procedures for law enforcement communication; CH31 operationalizes this by explaining the confidentiality constraints within those requests.
